idiom_name: Django MIDDLEWARE insertion + MiddlewareNotUsed / ASGI middleware stack
implementation_notes: In Django the route is the MIDDLEWARE list: append the audit middleware when the settings flag is on, or let the middleware decline itself by raising MiddlewareNotUsed in __init__ so one codebase runs with or without the detour. Each middleware receives get_response - the rest of the pipeline - and calling it is the rejoin to the destination; a detour that returns a response without calling get_response has become a filter, not a Detour. For ASGI stacks the same stage is a wrapper around the application callable appended conditionally at start-up.
pitfalls: MiddlewareNotUsed removes the stage from the chain entirely - a runtime toggle has to be checked inside __call__ instead.
MIDDLEWARE order is significant (authentication after sessions, and so on); inserting the detour at index 0 changes what the stage may assume about request state.
Mutating request.GET/POST in the detour prevents later views from modifying upload handlers, and short-circuiting (not calling get_response) makes the leg behaviourally different.
